docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
The essays in which a Victorian editor of The Economist set the dignified parts of the constitution (the Crown and the Lords) beside its efficient parts (the Cabinet and the House of Commons), and explained why the English system of government by a committee of Parliament differs from the American separation of powers.

From Standard Ebooks · CC0 1.0

Walter Bagehot (1826–1877), The English Constitution, 1867 (the text of the second edition, 1872). This book is not stored in this library: each chapter is read from the public repository of its Standard Ebooks edition when it is opened, shown in this library's format, and ends with its own attribution.
